task_instance: Given a small SPEC.md for a CLI task tracker (project/SPEC.md, created as sample input), run the planning-and-task-breakdown process: map the dependency graph, slice the work vertically per command, and produce tasks/plan.md (implementation plan with architecture decisions, phased task list, risks, open questions) and tasks/todo.md (the task list target, containing 5 tasks each with description, acceptance criteria, verification steps using the project's actual test command, dependencies, files touched, and estimated scope, plus 3 checkpoints between phases).
evidence: Created work dir with project/SPEC.md (sample 5-requirement CLI task tracker spec). Checked tasks/ was empty beforehand (no pre-existing incomplete plan to protect, per the skill's 'never overwrite' rule). Wrote tasks/plan.md (53 lines) following the Plan Document Template: Overview, Architecture Decisions, phased Task List (Foundation / Core Features / Polish) with checkpoints, Risks and Mitigations table, Open Questions, and a note on where tasks are tracked (no external tracker configured, so default tasks/todo.md convention applies, per the Output Files / Task List Target section). Wrote tasks/todo.md (146 lines) with 5 tasks (storage, add, list, done, CLI wiring) each following the Step 4 template exactly (Description, Acceptance criteria, Verification referencing `python3 -m unittest ...` which is a stdlib tool actually present -- confirmed `python3 --version` -> Python 3.11.15 -- Dependencies, Files likely touched, Estimated scope), plus 3 '## Checkpoint' sections between phases matching Step 5. Verified structure with grep: 5 '## Task' headers, 5 'Acceptance criteria' blocks, 5 'Verification:' blocks, 5 'Dependencies:' blocks, 3 '## Checkpoint' blocks -- matching every item in the skill's own Verification checklist (every task has acceptance criteria, every task has a verification step, dependencies identified, tasks recorded in the task list target, no task >5 files, checkpoints between phases). This is a pure planning/documentation deliverable (markdown files reasoned out from a spec); it required no network access, no credentials, and no tool beyond the shell and a text editor, all of which the offline runtime provides, so the skill's core intent is fully achievable here.
